# Volume 3 — Chapter XVI Adjusted Relationships

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“It’s the homiest spot I ever saw—it’s homier than home,” declared Cressida Lindsay, scanning her surroundings with eyes full of delight. Everyone was gathered as dusk fell in the large living-room at Tabby’s Place—Nell and Honora, Cressy and Mabel, Aunt Euphemia, Smudge, Joseph, the Sarah-Cat, and Gog and Magog. Across the walls, flickering shadows cast by the fire were dancing; purrs came from the cats; and, glowing through the golden dusk like creamy moons, stood a grand bowl of hothouse chrysanthemums that had been sent to Cressy by a victim.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0000 }

Twenty-one days had passed since they thought of themselves as established, and everyone was currently convinced that the trial would prove successful. A agreeable level of excitement had filled the initial fourteen days following their homecoming; they had kept themselves occupied placing their domestic possessions, arranging their modest home, and reconciling various viewpoints.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0001 }

Nell did not feel excessively grieved about departing from Brierley once it was time for her to go back to college. The final days of her holiday had been far from enjoyable. Island newspapers had printed her prize story; moreover, on his store counter, Mr. William Blair maintained a massive stack of pamphlets in pink, green, and yellow that held the tale, handing a copy to each buyer. After he dispatched a complimentary pack to Nell, she immediately threw every single one into the kitchen stove. Her feelings of shame stemmed solely from her personal standards, because the people of Brierley considered her winning the prize to be utterly grand. Honest admiration was felt for her by her numerous friends, whereas her small number of enemies viewed her with disdainful jealousy. Flossie Tulk remarked that she suspected Nell Harcourt had simply stolen the story, claiming certainty that she recalled seeing it in a publication years earlier. Having discovered or surmised that Wilfred had been rejected, the Motts remarked that they felt it was hardly a matter for pride, as nearly anyone could accomplish the same thing if she made an effort. Aunt Drusilla informed Nell that learning she had resorted to composing novels brought her great regret, adding that no person native to Brierley would engage in such a thing, and that this served as the result of taking in orphans from heaven knows where, whose parents possessed heaven knows what background. Even Mrs. Agatha Sowerby harbored gloomy doubts regarding the moral fitness of authoring fiction, even if that twenty-five dollar check nearly brought her around to accepting it.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0002 }

“The amount of money given for those falsehoods is truly astonishing, it really is,” she remarked, displaying a mixture of pride and sternness.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0003 }

Taking everything into account, the arrival of departure time brought a sense of relief. Furthermore, returning to Wexcombe felt delightful, being a knowledgeable, seasoned Soph surrounded by numerous companions welcoming one another on the lively first day. Nonie, Mabel, Hugh, and Wilfred Mott—who appeared more pompous than any Sophomore ever had previously—were present, alongside Cressy, whose Hector-and-Orlando debate remained unresolved, and Elias Purdy MacKinnon. Ever since departing Regent’s, Elias Purdy had worked as a schoolteacher, yet his mother decided that he ought to cease teaching at last and focus on studying for the ministry. Unfortunate Elias Purdy encountered misfortune right at the start of his university journey. A team of six merciless Sophs, living in the same boarding house, descended upon his room one evening and clipped the hair from one side of his head. The unfortunate Elias Purdy was forced to attend classes looking like this until his hair regenerated. He remarked to Nell with resentment that occasionally he questioned whether he actually possessed a true calling to become a minister.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0004 }

Aunt Euphemia delayed her arrival until the girls had prepared Tabby’s Place for her. A letter accompanied the key that Miss Tabby sent to Nell, stating that Gog and Magog were stored in a box beneath the spare-room bed, though they could be removed whenever desired; she appended a postscript expressing her hope that the girls would exercise care when hanging pictures. Five years prior, the living room had received new wallpaper, and she and Miss Maria desired that no more holes than were strictly required be punched into that fresh paper. Otherwise, she left all matters in Nell’s hands.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0005 }

What pleasure those girls derived from arranging their home! In the words of Cressy, it was nearly as delightful as a wedding. A person experienced the joy of creating a home minus the trouble of a spouse. Everyone carried an item along to decorate or add comfort to the small dwelling. Nonie and Cressy and Mabel possessed an abundance of ornaments and artwork, which they then hung based on their preferences, completely ignoring the new wallpaper of Miss Tabby.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0006 }

“We will fill the openings with putty upon our departure, dear—it will remain completely unknown to her,” they remarked to Nell, who was objecting.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0007 }

Nell was given a pine needle cushion by Isolde, while a fearfully and wonderfully embroidered cushion was presented to both her and Honora by Miss Ada. A large box of preserves had been sent by Thirza, who also made dark hints about a Thanksgiving hamper, and a patchwork quilt was given to Nell by Mrs. Sowerby, who additionally lent her five others.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0008 }

“You take them,” she instructed with authority. “There is no reason for them to be stored in that garret trunk for moths to chew when they could be utilized instead.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0009 }

Moths would not have dared approach those quilts, because the smell of mothballs on them was so strong that two whole weeks hanging in the orchard at Tabby’s Place were required before anyone could bear them inside the house. Indeed, the refined Linden Avenue had seldom seen a sight quite like it. The stern elderly millionaire residing "next door" walked over with the desire to purchase the magnificent red and yellow "tulip-pattern" quilt that Mrs. Agatha had bestowed upon Nell. He explained that his mother used to create similar quilts, and by Jove, he desired one so he could remember her. Nell refused to sell her quilt, which disappointed him greatly, but she penned a full account of the incident to Mrs. Sowerby. Upon hearing this, the delighted lady sent a reply stating she possessed an identical extra quilt, allowing the tobacco king to obtain his quilt in the end, and he demanded that it be placed upon his bed, which appalled his stylish wife.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0010 }

Mrs. Sowerby’s quilts proved extremely helpful during that winter. Despite possessing numerous virtues, Tabby’s Place was not without its defects. It was actually quite a chilly residence; thus, as the freezing nights arrived, the girls felt extremely happy to nestle beneath Mrs. Sowerby’s quilts, wishing that lending them would be remembered as a virtuous deed. Nell occupied the blue room she had desired from the moment she saw it. Honora and Mabel were in the big room. Cressy felt completely delighted with the small room situated above the kitchen; while Aunt Euphemia was designated to occupy the ground-floor room adjacent to the living-room. Initially, Smudge made his bed on the doorstep.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0011 }

Returning from Wexcombe several days later, Nell, as she walked toward her house, noticed that she was receiving secretive, fond grins from the folk she encountered. What could be wrong with her, Nell pondered with apprehension. Had her hat gone askew? Was her belt untied? Twisting her neck to check herself, Nell, finally, caught sight of Smudge.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0012 }

Trotting along behind her, near her heels, was easily the most miserable example of the cat family she had ever seen. The creature was far beyond kittenhood, gangly, skinny, and scruffy-looking. Portions of its ears were missing, one eye was presently out of order, and its jowl was swollen in a laughable manner. Regarding its shade, had a cat that was formerly black been completely and thoroughly scorched, the outcome would have matched the tone of this stray’s sparse, wet, unattractive coat.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0013 }

Nell attempted to "shoo" him away, yet the cat refused to "shoo." For as long as she remained standing, he remained seated upon his haunches and stared at her in a reproachful manner using his single functional eye; whenever she started walking again, he trailed behind. Nell accepted his presence beside her right up to the moment she arrived at the entrance of Tabby’s Place, a gate she unkindly closed right in front of him, foolishly assuming she was done with him forever. However, when Cressy held the door open fifteen minutes afterward, the cat of a rusty-brown shade was waiting right on the step. Furthermore, he immediately rushed inside and jumped onto Nell’s lap, uttering a "miaow" that sounded partly begging and partly victorious.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0014 }

“Nell,” Mabel said in a severe tone, “is that animal yours?”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0015 }

“No, I do not,” objected revolted Nell. “The beast trailed me back from somewhere. It was impossible for me to shake him off. Ugh, get down. Decent cats are reasonably acceptable to me; however, beasties with your coloring do not appeal to me.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0016 }

Pussy, on the other hand, declined to descend. He unconcernedly coiled himself into Nell's lap and started purring.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0017 }

“It is clear he has chosen you as his own,” Honora chuckled.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0018 }

“I will NOT be adopted,” Nell declared with insistence.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0019 }

“The poor creature is starving,” Cressy said with pity. “Why, his skin is nearly pierced by his bones.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0020 }

“Indeed, I will provide him with a full meal, after which he has to go back to his original location,” Nell declared with determination.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0021 }

The cat received food and was placed outside. Upon the arrival of morning, he remained located on the doorstep. He persisted in sitting on the doorstep, rushing inside every time someone opened the door. Not even the slightest chilly reception impacted him; he paid no attention to anyone except Nell. Driven by pity, the girls gave him food; however, once seven days went by, they concluded that action needed to be taken. The cat looked better. Normalcy had returned to his eye and cheek; his thinness was slightly reduced; and someone had observed him cleaning his face.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0022 }

“Even so, we are unable to retain him,” Mabel stated. “Aunt Phemie arrives the following week, bringing along the Sarah-cat. Having two cats is impossible for us; besides, should we attempt it, this Smudge Coat would engage in constant battles with the Sarah-cat. Combat is inherent to his character. Yesterday night, he engaged in a fierce war against the tobacco-king’s cat, completely vanquishing him, horse, foot and artillery.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0023 }

“It is necessary that we dispose of him,” concurred Nell, glaring grimly at the topic of their conversation, who was vibrating with a purr on the fireside mat, appearing as gentle as a lamb. “The issue, however, remains—in what manner? By what means can four defenseless women dispose of a feline that refuses to be disposed of?”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0024 }

“It is necessary that we chloroform him,” Cressy remarked briskly. “That represents the most humane approach.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0025 }

“Does any single one of us understand how to give a cat chloroform?” Nell inquired in a dismal tone.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0026 }

“I truly do, sweetheart. Being able to do this is among my rare—regrettably rare—practical skills. Back home, I have gotten rid of a number of them. In the morning, you collect the cat and feed him a hearty meal. Next, you fetch a former burlap sack—you can find one on the back porch—place the cat upon it, and cover him with an inverted wooden box. After that, obtain a two-ounce container of chloroform, remove its cork, and slide it beneath the box's rim. Place a substantial weight onto the upper part of the box and do not disturb it until nightfall. The cat will have passed away, resting curled up calmly just as though he were sleeping. There is no pain—no fighting.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0027 }

“That seems simple,” Nell remarked with doubt.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0028 }

“There is nothing to it. Simply entrust the matter to me. I will make sure it is handled,” Cressy said in a reassuring tone.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0029 }

Thus the chloroform was obtained, and Smudge was enticed to his death the following morning. Having eaten his breakfast and licked his chops, he scrambled onto Nell’s lap. Nell felt a pang of doubt. She was loved and trusted by this poor animal. In what way could she participate in this slaughter?
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0030 }

“Take him, here,” she told Cressy hurriedly. “A murderess is what I feel like.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0031 }

“You know he won’t suffer,” Cressy offered by way of comfort, yet Nell had already run away.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0032 }

Within the back porch, the deadly act took place. On that day, no one approached the area. However, as twilight fell, Cressy announced the necessity of burying Smudge.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0033 }

“The digging of his grave in the orchard must be done by Nonie and Mabel,” stated Cressy, “and I need Nell to accompany me to carry the box away. It is that specific task that I constantly abhor.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0034 }

The pair of plotters walked on tiptoe unwillingly toward the rear veranda. With great care, Cressy raised the rock that she had placed upon the crate. At that moment, weak yet clear, an indisputable meow echoed beneath the crate.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0035 }

“He—he isn’t dead,” Nell gasped, sitting down on the doorstep of the kitchen with a blank look.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0036 }

“It cannot be otherwise,” Cressy stated, unable to believe it.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0037 }

A second faint cry confirmed his continued existence. A mutual gaze passed between the pair of young women.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0038 }

“What steps shall we take?” asked Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0039 }

“Why on earth aren’t you coming?” asked Mabel, showing up at the entrance. “The grave is prepared by us. ‘What silent still and silent all?’” she mockingly quoted.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0040 }

“‘Indeed, no, the speech of those who have passed resembles the remote rush of a waterfall,’” Nell immediately replied with a quotation of her own, gesturing with gravity toward the chest.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0041 }

The strain was dispelled by an eruption of giggles.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0042 }

“We have to leave him in this place until the morning,” Cressy said, putting the stone back into position. “For five minutes now, he has not made a sound. It could be that those noises we caught were his last dying gasp. Otherwise, beneath the pressure of our remorseful minds, we might have simply fancied them.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0043 }

However, upon the removal of the box that morning, Smudge leaped with a single joyful bound onto Nell’s shoulder, whereupon he started lovingly licking her face. No cat had ever been more undeniably full of life.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0044 }

“There is a knot hole in the box right here,” Cressy groaned. “It escaped my notice. The reason he failed to die is that. Re-doing everything is what we must do now.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0045 }

“No, we haven’t,” Nell abruptly proclaimed. “Smudge will not be slain another time. He belongs to me—and you simply must accept it.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0046 }

“Oh, well, provided you arrange things with Aunt Phemie and the Sarah-cat,” Mabel said, speaking like someone disclaiming all further responsibility for the matter.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0047 }

Since that moment Smudge belonged to the household. Nightly, he rested upon the scrubbing cushion located in the rear porch and feasted upon the best food available. When Aunt Euphemia arrived, he had become chubby, shiny, and fairly presentable. Nevertheless, similar to the cat of Kipling, he “walked by himself.” Every cat's paw opposed him, just as his own paw opposed every cat. Gradually, he defeated the high-class cats inhabiting Linden Avenue. Regarding people, his affection belonged exclusively to Nell. No other person attempted to pet him. A furious spit alongside a noise resembling highly inappropriate words met whoever tried it.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0048 }

“The pretensiousness that cat displays is entirely unbearable,” stated Mabel.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0049 }

“He was a pleasant old cat, he was,” affirmed Nell, stubbornly hugging her animal.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0050 }

“Indeed, I am unsure how he and the Sarah-cat will manage to co-exist,” Mabel remarked with pessimism. “Feline battles occurring in the orchard during the night are troublesome enough. However, feline battles right here in the livingroom cannot be tolerated.” Eventually, Aunt Euphemia made her appearance. Nell, Honora, and Cressy had anticipated her coming with some apprehension; yet, once Aunt Euphemia was settled in the rocking chair facing the burning hearth, they metaphorically prostrated themselves and revered her.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0051 }

Small and elderly, Aunt Euphemia possessed a diminutive face that was gently triangular, along with big, tender blue eyes possessing an irrepressible youthfulness and brimming with as many expectations as those of a young maiden. Her cheeks were rose-colored, and her silver-white hair was arranged in charming, small rolls above her ears.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0052 }

“It is quite an outmoded method,” she remarked, busily working her needles on an item as delicate and rosy as an evening cloud. “However, I am outmoded myself. My garments are, and naturally my views are as well. Remember, I am not claiming they are superior because of it. Indeed, I suppose they are likely much inferior. Nevertheless, they have proven quite comfortable through use. Fresh footwear looks finer than worn footwear, yet the worn footwear feels more pleasant. I have reached an age where I can pamper myself regarding footwear and views. My intention is to be very relaxed here. I am aware you anticipate that I will supervise you and maintain your propriety, yet I refuse. If you will ever understand how to conduct yourselves, you are at an age to know it now. Therefore, as it pertains to me,” Aunt Euphemia finished, a gleam present in her youthful eyes, “you are all free to ruin yourselves as you see fit.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0053 }

“Oh, won't someone divide those cats?” Mabel implored, shuddering.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0054 }

Not only the Sarah-cat but also Joseph was brought along by Aunt Euphemia. Joseph, as she clarified, used to belong to a cherished friend of hers who had relocated to Vancouver.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0055 }

“She was unable to bring Joseph along, which led her to entreat me to keep him. Refusing her was truly not an option for me. He is a wonderful cat—or rather, his temperament is wonderful. She gave him the name Joseph owing to his multicolored coat.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0056 }

That was undoubtedly true. As Mabel remarked in disgust, Joseph resembled a mobile bag of rags. The base shade of his coat could not be determined. White adorned his legs, which were marked by black spots. A large yellow swatch on one flank and a black one on the opposite side sat upon his gray back. Yellow comprised his tail, except for its gray end. One of his ears was black, whereas the other was yellow. Because a black patch covered one eye, he possessed an intensely devil-may-care appearance. Actually, he possessed a gentle, harmless, and friendly nature. Joseph resembled a lily of the field in a single way, even if in no other. He did not labor, nor did he spin, nor did he hunt mice. Nevertheless, Solomon, despite all his splendor, did not rest upon cushions that were softer, nor did he indulge more completely in rich foods.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0057 }

Delivered via express, Joseph and the Sarah-cat came in individual crates. Following their uncrating and a meal, Joseph chose the particular cushion and spot that suited his fancy, whereas the Sarah-cat quietly took a seat in front of the hearth and began cleaning her face. A giant, smooth, gray-and-white feline, she possessed a massive self-respect that was in no way diminished by any awareness of her lowborn roots. Aunt Euphemia had received her as a gift from her laundress.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0058 }

“Because her name was Sarah, puss was always referred to as the Sarah-cat by my husband,” Aunt Euphemia clarified. “Being eight years old, she is an extraordinary mouser. Have no fear, Mabel. Fighting is something the Sarah-cat never does and Joseph seldom.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0059 }

“Out of self-defense, they will be forced to fight at this spot,” Mabel remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0060 }

Right at this point, Smudge came into view. He leaped with glee to the middle of the chamber prior to spotting the unwanted guests. Thereupon he froze instantly; his tail swelled to thrice its normal size. The hair along his spine stood erect in a hostile curve; Smudge dipped his head, let out a terrifying scream of rage and resistance, and hurled himself toward the Sarah-cat.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0061 }

The grand creature had ceased cleaning her face to observe him with curiosity. A single disdainful swat from her skilled paw countered his charge. Tumbling uncontrollably onto the rug, Smudge gathered himself in a daze. What manner of feline was she to have cuffed his ears? Dubiously, he gazed at the Sarah-cat. Should he try again, or should he refrain? Turning her back on him on purpose, the Sarah-cat restarted her grooming. Smudge chose to refrain. He failed to ever try again. Starting from that moment, the Sarah-cat was in complete control. Smudge did not ever bother her again.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0062 }

However, Joseph unwisely sat upright and yawned. Smudge, eager to pay back his humiliation, launched himself at him. Though Joseph possessed a peaceful disposition, he was capable of fighting, and fighting effectively, when required. A succession of indecisive clashes followed. Smudge and Joseph engaged in combat whenever they saw one another daily. Nell sided with Smudge and loathed Joseph. Mabel felt hopeless. Aunt Euphemia, on the other hand, merely chuckled.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0063 }

“Allow them to settle it themselves,” she remarked with indulgence. “They will become friendly before long. Joseph requires some activity—he was becoming excessively overweight. Meanwhile, Smudge must realize that he is not the sole cat in existence.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0064 }

In time, Joseph and Smudge resigned themselves to the state of affairs, transforming from bitter foes into devoted companions. Resting upon one shared pillow, they entwined their paws and solemnly licked one another’s faces clean.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0065 }

“Everyone has become accustomed to one another,” Cressy remarked. “Also, cleaning dishes and sweeping floors are skills I have acquired.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0066 }

“However, you do not have to attempt to convince us of your ability to chloroform a cat,” Nell chuckled.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0067 }

“The knothole was entirely to blame,” Cressy objected.
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0068 }

“That the knothole existed was fortunate,” Aunt Euphemia remarked with a somewhat stern tone. “The drowning of kittens is a necessity, I acknowledge, or else the earth would become overcrowded. However, no respectable, fully grown cat ought to be killed—except if he consumes eggs.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0069 }

“If you had witnessed Smudge upon his arrival at this place, you would not have deemed him particularly presentable,” Mabel remarked. “He truly resembled the Old Nick.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0070 }

“I do not think the Devil could be quite so unattractive,” Aunt Euphemia remarked thoughtfully. “He would fail to cause as much damage were that the case. My impression of him has always been that of an attractive gentleman.”
{: #nw-v03-c16-p0071 }
